items.title: Load the Desk article's reader-interaction scripts after first paint
items.why: Every Desk article ships eleven deferred scripts ahead of a text LCP. CI result files from S372 and S373 show observed FCP equal to observed LCP, steady simulated FCP and a simulated LCP that swings 2.3s to 3.9s depending on how many scripts finished before the paint. Reactions, presence, comments, the CSRF token and Turnstile all serve content below the article body.
items.recipe: Add a small shell asset that requests those scripts, in their current order, once the first paint has happened or the reader interacts. Emit it from generate-news-pages in place of the five deferred tags. Keep the Trusted Types policy pattern the homepage loader uses. Regenerate news pages and shell assets through the build. Add a unit test for the emitted markup and a browser spec that proves reactions and comments still mount and that the scripts are requested after first paint.
items.stageRationale: A required check that fails on unchanged bytes blocks every production promotion.
items.informationFindingOutcome: A reader sees the article text with fewer requests competing for it, and reactions and comments are ready by the time they scroll to them.
items.acceptance: Unit and browser specs pass; reactions and comments mount on a generated article; the article Lighthouse runs on the pushed commit pass their unchanged floors without a re-run.

premises.claim: The article template emits the Desk interaction scripts as deferred tags

L1.recipe: Move only Turnstile and the CSRF token behind interaction.

L2.recipe: One post-paint loader for all five scripts, generator change, unit and browser coverage.

L3.recipe: Mount each widget on visibility with an intersection observer and per-widget loading states.

executionLog.note: Implemented and verified locally: four scripts parked on Desk pages (presence kept eager because it times the visit). Unit 10/10; browser spec 3/3 on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; reactions and comments mount. Acceptance still open: the article Lighthouse runs on the pushed commit.

Acceptance met on the pushed commit: the measured article scored 0.98, 0.99, 0.99 against the unchanged 0.90 floor on the first attempt. Verified on staging and production with the browser spec (9/9 each).

items.title: Move the homepage's non-visual deferred scripts behind first paint
items.why: The homepage loads 28 deferred scripts and scores 0.75 to 0.78 against a 0.76 floor. Several of them measure, track or enhance content that is below the fold or invisible, and need nothing before the first paint.
items.recipe: Classify each deferred homepage script by whether it changes pixels above the fold. Leave those in place. Load the rest, in their current order, from a post-paint stage in the existing homepage loader, after confirming each one initialises correctly when it runs after DOMContentLoaded. Measure layout shift before and after in a browser on desktop and mobile.
items.stageRationale: The homepage is the page that most often fails the required check.
items.informationFindingOutcome: The homepage hero and its primary actions are ready sooner; tracking and below-the-fold enhancements follow without changing what the visitor sees.
items.acceptance: No new console errors; layout shift not worse than before on desktop and mobile; moved scripts still run; the homepage Lighthouse runs on the pushed commit pass the unchanged 0.76 floor without a re-run.

premises.claim: The homepage carries more than twenty deferred script tags

L2.recipe: Classify all deferred scripts, move every non-visual one, verify initialisation and layout shift.

L3.recipe: Bundle the above-the-fold scripts into one file and load everything else on visibility.

executionLog.note: Implemented and verified locally: seven of 28 homepage scripts parked; consent banner, hero scripts, click tracking and error reporting kept eager. Layout shift unchanged (at or below 0.008 before and after, desktop and mobile). Acceptance still open: the homepage Lighthouse runs on the pushed commit.

Acceptance met on the pushed commit: the homepage scored 0.81, 0.95, 0.98 against the unchanged 0.76 floor on the first attempt. Blocking time now appears after first paint (106 to 665 ms across runs); stability across releases remains to be observed.

items.title: Spell out Synthetic Intelligence (SI) where the site first uses the abbreviation
items.why: The shared Resources menu shows the label 'AI vs. SI Explained' on 257 pages before any page expands the abbreviation. CANON-056 and CANON-030 require the expansion on first use. One FAQ question on /synthetic-intelligence/ is also read by the checker as a superintelligence claim.
items.recipe: Change the neighbouring menu label in config/resource-links.json to 'Synthetic Intelligence (SI)' so the expansion precedes the abbreviation everywhere the menu renders, and propagate through the navigation generator. Reword the FAQ question so it asks about Super Intelligence without the adjective the checker treats as a claim. Recapture the menu on desktop and mobile in every theme.
items.stageRationale: A STRONG canon gap on every public page.
items.informationFindingOutcome: A visitor meeting the abbreviation in the menu sees what it stands for beside it.
items.acceptance: check-si-terminology reports conform; the menu fits on desktop and mobile in every theme.

premises.claim: The shared menu label uses the bare abbreviation

L2.recipe: Rename, propagate, reword the FAQ question, recapture the menu in every theme.

L3.recipe: Add the terminology checker to build:check with a per-page first-use test.

executionLog.note: Menu label changed in config/resource-links.json and propagated; check-si-terminology 258 findings to 2, both accepted in D-S374.3. One line and unclipped on desktop and mobile in all seven themes. FAQ question reworded, answer unchanged.

items.title: Make the stats-surface canon posture true
items.why: The CANON-054 checker reports 'no /stats route'. S368 deliberately retired /stats/ into /evidence/#numbers with a 301, so the surface exists and the checker cannot see it. Meanwhile context/CANON_ADOPTION.md records CANON-054 and CANON-055 as 'adopted (suggested) — Conformance checker passed: }' although both checkers exit 1. One published project count below five carries no explicit clearance.
items.recipe: Do not rebuild the retired page. Mark the project count as an explicitly cleared small count in build-stats-surface (it counts public projects, not people). Record the STRONG-gap justification for the retired route in DECISIONS. Ship one Ark report to studio-ops covering the checker's missing successor-route support and the adoption writer that records a failed checker as passed.
items.stageRationale: A posture file that records a failing check as passed misleads every later session.
items.informationFindingOutcome: The published project count carries its privacy clearance, and the next session reads the true state of the stats canon.
items.acceptance: The small-count warning is gone; DECISIONS carries the justification; Ark cargo is shipped with its id recorded.
